title: Post-Cold War Order: US Hegemony and Russia

scenes.text: Why did Cold War peace quickly turn into a new global rivalry?
scenes.narration: Imagine celebrating the end of an old fight, only to find yourself facing new rivals right away. After the Soviet collapse, America claimed absolute leadership, but Russia soon pushed back.

scenes.text: A dominant school prefect expanding rules until a former topper pushes back.
scenes.narration: Think of this like a school analogy. Imagine one dominant head boy running every club unchallenged, until the former topper feels cornered and rebels to reclaim his lost respect.

scenes.name: Madeleine Albright
scenes.idea: The United States is the indispensable nation guiding world affairs.
scenes.narration: Former US Secretary of State Madeleine Albright called America the indispensable nation. Washington believed it had a unique destiny to lead global trade, secure oceans, and shape world politics.

scenes.heading: US Hegemony Versus Russian Power

columns.title: Russia
items: Equal natural resources and space technology
Holds ICBMs and permanent UNSC seat
Seeks Russia China India strategic axis

scenes.narration: Here's the trick to understanding their rivalry. America sought to control oceans and contain challengers through an Asia Pivot, while Russia retained matching resources, nuclear missiles, and veto power.

scenes.heading: Key Turning Points In Relations

events.what: NATO expands eastward despite Russian objections
United States exits Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty
Russia intervenes in Georgia over South Ossetia

scenes.narration: Watch how trust broke down over time. Moscow viewed NATO's eastward expansion as a broken promise, leading from the 2008 Georgia intervention straight to the 2014 Crimea crisis.

scenes.heading: Debate Over Cold War 2.0
items: Dmitri Trenin terms current friction Cold War 2.0
Modern Russia lacks the Soviet ideological mission
Moscow offers no alternative universal world order
scenes.narration: Scholar Dmitri Trenin calls this friction Cold War 2.0. However, other scholars disagree because modern Russia lacks Soviet communist ideology and does not offer an alternative global order.

items: America pursued global primacy as the indispensable nation.
NATO expansion eastward triggered sharp Russian pushback.
Nuclear parity and geopolitical clashes sustain a new rivalry.
scenes.narration: Remember three key ideas: America pursued unchallenged primacy, NATO's eastward push sparked deep Russian resentment, and unresolved geopolitical clashes continue to drive their tense rivalry.
